sentences.text: Anuradha Chadda vs Rakesh Gupta on 13 September, 2024

Author: Rahul Bharti Bench: Rahul Bharti  Serial No. 12  HIGH COURT OF JAMMU & KASHMIR AND LADAKH  AT JAMMU Case:- MA No. 120/2015 Anuradha Chadda, aged 51 years W/o Sh. Jatinder Chadda R/o House No. 2, Gurah Bakshi Nagar,
Jammu. .....Appellant(s)/Petitioner(s)
 Through: Mr. R. K. S. Thakur, Advocate.

Vs 1. Rakesh Gupta, S/o Sh. Kaka Ram,
 R/o Talab Tillo, Jammu, C/o Vikas  Motor, Channi Chouwadhi, Jammu.
2. Sudershan Kumar Chopra, S/o Hira  Nand, R/o Lakhdata Bazar, Jammu.
..... Respondent(s)
Through: None.

Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAHUL BHARTI, JUDGE  ORDER (13.09.2024)
1. Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu in a claim petition on file No. 356/Claim instituted on 06.08.2004 came to award compensation of an amount of Rs. 1,85,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% from the date of filing of the claim petition in favour of the claimant-Rakesh Gupta S/o Kaka Ram R/o Talab Tillo, Jammu.

2. The liability to pay the compensation stood fastened upon the respondents, namely, Anuradha Chopra (Chadda),-the owner and Sudershan Kumar Chopra-the driver of scooter-JK02A-8504.
3.
Owner Anuradha Chopra (Chadda) came forward with the present appeal instituted on 16.03.2015.

Anuradha Chadda vs Rakesh Gupta on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89770009/
1 4.

Since the impugned award is ex parte against the said two persons namely, owner and the driver,
as such, the owner came forward with an application for setting aside the ex parte award before the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu which, by virtue of an order dated 28.02.2015,
refused to set aside the award resulting in presentation of the present appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
5.

In terms of an order dated 30.03.2015, the appellant was directed to deposit 75% of the awarded compensation amount which, accordingly, came to be deposited with the Registry with an amount of Rs. 1,38,750/- on 29.04.2015.
6. Service of the claimant-Rakesh Gupta has been a bottleneck in the present case ever since its institution.

Ultimately, the counsel for the appellant came to apprise this court that as per information the respondent No. 1-Rakesh Gupta has demised and despite best efforts, the appellant is not able to procure the knowledge of the legal representatives of the respondent No. 1-Rakesh Gupta.

7. On 13.12.2023 the fact about death of the respondent No. 1- Rakesh Gupta was shared by learned counsel for the appellant with this court and now more than nine months have gone by without any application for bringing on record the legal representatives of the deceased-respondent No.
1-Rakesh Gupta having taken place, as such, this appeal abates.

8. The amount deposited by the appellant, in terms of order dated 30.03.2015 lying with this court,
is directed to be remitted back along with interest to the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal(MACT),
Jammu for the sake of its payment to the legal representatives, if any, of the deceased claimant-Rakesh Gupta coming forward.

9. The dismissal of this appeal as being abated will not prejudice the appellant to seek revival of the appeal in case, if any, legal representatives of deceased/respondent No. 1-Rakesh Gupta comes forward with an execution for payment of remainder amount of compensation before the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal(MACT), Jammu.

10. In the event, any legal representative of the deceased/respondent No. 1-Rakesh Gupta S/o Kaka Ram, R/o Talab Tillo, Jammu comes forward for seeking release of the amount to be transmitted in terms of this order from this court to the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu, then before ordering the release of the amount, the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT), Jammu also to notify the appellant.
11. Till its claim by any legal representation of the deceased/respondent No. 1-Rakesh Gupta, the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT),
Jammu shall, upon receipt, keep the amount in a fixed deposit.
12. Disposed of.

(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 13.09.2024 Shivalee
